v8g_key_results.interpretation: No internal numerical contradiction was found between the published transfer and component checks, but the controlling margin is small and the check is not independent of the NIST global model.

v8h_key_results.interpretation: Mechanically bounded local beam networks did not sustain the late-time synthetic-extrema ensemble. This does not contradict the NIST global model because the V8H-A model omits the mechanically explicit composite slab path that NIST relied on, and the as-built beam/connection schedules remain unavailable.

v8i_key_results.interpretation: The bounded reinforcement-only catenary did not restore equilibrium, including in the deliberately optimistic cold upper envelope. Because the same reduced network also fails the 20 C post-impact baseline while WTC 1 remained standing for 102 min, V8I-A is falsified as a standalone real load-path model. The 100 percent synthetic failure fraction is not an event probability and cannot support a demolition inference.

v8j_key_results.interpretation: V8J localizes the cold failure to a topology cut rather than a first global core overload. Published component capacities do not specify a surviving compatible force-displacement bridge across that cut, so the cold gate remains unvalidated. This is a limitation of the reduced model, not evidence for demolition or against the observed post-impact stability.

v8k_key_results.source_figure: NIST NCSTAR 1-6C Figure 5-59(b), Floor 96 Case Ai impact-damaged core-beam model
v8k_key_results.interpretation: The official-model figure rejects the local Floor 96 core-beam path as a standalone repair for V8J: three loaded removed nodes have no visible surviving route. The remaining 505 route also fails the inherited proxy envelope, but its as-built capacity is unknown. Because NIST applied no vertical top-of-column loads in this subsystem and used Case Ai rather than refined Case A/B damage, the result requires a multistory/global path audit and is not a contradiction of observed stability or evidence of demolition.

v8l_key_results.interpretation: The six-level core-only model loses equilibrium in all 36 cold cases. The NIST moment-connected subnetwork is topologically insufficient by itself; even the strongest reconstructed orthogonal upper envelope reaches only 78 percent of the prescribed core demand before a loaded component disconnects at 79 percent. This is qualitatively consistent with NIST's non-convergent isolated Case B core and identifies the missing core-office-floor-perimeter and/or hat-truss coupling; it is not an event probability or demolition evidence.

v8m_key_results.interpretation: No force-displacement case retaining the published 44-kip interior horizontal seat limit transfers the 4,772-kip V8L component at or below the 25-in significant-floor-displacement reference. Even an intact four-face, six-floor envelope requires 79.5 in; the north-damage-informed four-face case requires 110.1 in. An uncapped linear-elastic shell closes the path at 11.4 in, demonstrating sensitivity to the unpublished equivalent membrane stiffness and omitted connection failure rather than validating a physical path. The perimeter prototype reserve is not controlling, and the cold hat-truss credit remains zero.

v8n_key_results.interpretation: The inverse surrogate predicts the held-out floor totals well and has low mean held-out DCR error, but it misses the localized Column 804 response beyond the predeclared maximum-error gate and selects zero global mixing. It therefore cannot repair the V8L/V8M cold path as a predictive model. Agreement remains dependent on NIST outputs and is not independent validation or demolition evidence.

v8o_key_results.interpretation: Direct vector digitization of the Floor 98 bubble map supports a compact anisotropic fit and low mean cross-figure DCR error, but the model misses localized responses at Columns 705, 804 and 605 beyond the predeclared maximum-error gates. The bubble legend also implies an absolute core total inconsistent with Table 4-20, so only relative areas normalized to the table are used. A single-level anisotropic kernel is not predictive across Floors 93-99; the result remains a NIST-output emulator, not independent event validation or demolition evidence.

v8p_key_results.interpretation: The bounded raster digitization is internally consistent with Table 4-20 and the V8O Floor 98 vector map, but a vertically continuous smooth graph cannot predict the localized 605 and 804 load peaks. Three selected parameters lie on grid boundaries and 101 near-equivalent cases span most parameter ranges. V8P therefore establishes non-identifiability of the smooth interpolator and does not validate a cold load path, independent event mechanism, probability, or demolition hypothesis.

v8q_key_results.interpretation: The explicit floor-by-floor graph can satisfy every published total and nodal balance exactly, but this is enabled by 24 uncalibrated boundary ports and a 56-dimensional structural null space. All 103 flow components have null-space support, so their raw mathematical ranges are unbounded without constitutive laws. The new six-column blind test covers only 40.5 percent of intervals and exceeds the 450-kip maximum-error gate. V8Q therefore establishes algebraic feasibility but neither predictive nor mechanical identification; it does not authorize thermal/Blender coupling or support an explosive/thermite inference.

v8r_key_results.interpretation: No mapped bounded V8L/V8M proxy case satisfies even one complete V8P floor interval set. Opening both internal and external unknown paths restores exact feasibility at all seven floors, while multiplying the optimistic mapped edge and port envelopes jointly requires factors from 1.94 to 8.15, with Floor 96 controlling. This identifies missing or insufficient reduced-model capacity, not falsified NIST data, event probability, demolition evidence, or authority for thermal/Blender coupling.

v8s_key_results.interpretation: V8S freezes source/page-traceable AA11 mass, video kinematics, damage-refined reproduction inputs, tower geometry and eight validation metrics. The input-only tail-clearance estimate agrees with the approximately 0.25 s NIST scale within 0.010 s, but this validates only geometric timing. NIST refined orientation and position from the observed facade damage, no qualified global high-rate explicit solver is installed, and the as-built impact-zone mesh is incomplete. V8S therefore does not validate penetration damage, fire, collapse or an explosive/thermite mechanism, and Blender/thermal coupling remains unauthorized.

v8t_key_results.interpretation: The official TWISBEAM smoke model completes normally and reproduces the published cycle-16750 record exactly, qualifying the local OpenRadioss executable chain and a basic shell-element regression. The isolated runtime only avoids an incompatible 2017 system OpenMP DLL and does not modify the downloaded package or System32. V8T does not yet qualify WTC material, contact, rate, rupture, erosion, mesh, energy, impact, fire, collapse, explosive or thermite physics.

v8u_key_results.interpretation: All six rigid-sphere and shell-panel surrogate cases terminate normally with zero added mass and zero hourglass energy, and the one-thread versus four-thread baseline is exactly repeatable. The medium-to-fine residual speed changes by only 0.41 percent, but contact impulse changes by 20.9 percent and fails the predeclared 10 percent convergence gate. The truncated panel and rigid sphere are qualification surrogates, not a reproduction of a JT9D, aircraft breakup, global WTC impact, fire, collapse, explosive, or thermite mechanism.

v8v_key_results.interpretation: All seven V8V runs terminate normally, preserve V8U exactly, add no meaningful mass, show zero hourglass energy, pass the half-time-step, momentum-balance, rupture-ordering and thread-repeatability checks, but fail the energy, nominal projectile mass-retention and 50-to-25 mm impulse gates. At the first 50 and 25 mm records, before facade FNZ activates, elastic contact energy is already nonzero and enormous, localizing a mesh-dependent projectile self-contact initialization instability. Therefore the 50 and 25 mm impulses and fragment velocities are not physical results. V8V qualifies neither a JT9D, a global WTC impact, fire, collapse, explosive or thermite physics, nor Blender as physical validation.

v8w_key_results.interpretation: V8W removes the V8V pre-impact numerical instability. All 100, 50 and 25 mm free-flight cases have exactly zero contact energy, pairwise impulse, erosion, mass change, energy error and momentum change. All facade cases then terminate normally with zero pre-impact contact energy, no meaningful added mass, zero hourglass energy, at most 1.75 percent absolute energy error, 97.6 percent nominal projectile mass retention, correct rupture ordering, 1.07 percent half-time-step sensitivity and exact thread repeatability. The only failed facade gate is the unchanged 10 percent impulse-convergence criterion: the 50-to-25 mm difference remains 32.87 percent. V8W therefore fixes contact initialization but does not qualify the facade-impact impulse, a JT9D, the whole aircraft, global WTC impact, fire, collapse, explosive or thermite physics, or Blender as physical validation.

v8x_key_results.interpretation: V8X isolates facade and projectile mesh effects and compares them with a numerical control that practically disables LAW2 erosion. The eroding cases remain strongly mesh-sensitive, while the non-eroding 100/50/25 mm diagonal gives 357.920, 363.524 and 356.569 kN-s and passes the unchanged 10 percent gate with a 1.951 percent 50-to-25 mm difference. Within this tested surrogate, the principal diagnosed driver is the unregularized strain-to-failure erosion. Removing rupture is not physical validation; the deformable projectile-facade subassembly, JT9D, whole aircraft and global WTC impact remain unqualified, and Blender remains visualization only.

v8y_key_results.interpretation: All seven V8Y cases terminate normally and pass the predeclared numerical gates. With /FAIL/JOHNSON plus /NONLOCAL/MAT, the 50-to-25 mm facade-contact impulse difference falls to 8.34 percent, below the unchanged 10 percent gate; final projectile momentum differs by 1.55 percent, half-time-step impulse sensitivity is 0.051 percent, and one-to-four-thread results match exactly. The 100-to-50 mm impulse difference remains 33.43 percent. LeMAX=100 mm and the constant failure strains remain declared numerical hypotheses rather than measured JT9D, cowling or panel-124 fracture properties. V8Y therefore qualifies only this reduced numerical subassembly; physical failure-parameter identification, whole-aircraft and global WTC impact physics remain unqualified, and Blender remains visualization only.

v8z_key_results.interpretation: V8Z verifies the declared official-source files and preserves V8W through V8Y. Both new 50 mm cases terminate normally and, together with the cached V8Y LeMAX=100 mm reference, pass the contact, energy, mass, momentum-balance, rupture and solver-length checks. The maximum pairwise facade-contact impulse difference across LeMAX=50/100/200 mm is 37.84 percent and the maximum final-projectile-momentum difference is 11.95 percent, both above the unchanged 10 percent gates. The conditional fine cases are therefore not executed. The NIST and method sources do not identify representative WTC-steel or engine/cowling fracture surfaces or a physical internal length. V8Z is a valid negative sensitivity result, not a solver failure and not physical validation of the impact; global, thermal, Blender, explosive and thermite gates remain closed.

v9a_key_results.interpretation: V9A reproduces all four published NCSTAR 1-3D log-log strength-rate slopes from 12 tabulated observations for the M26 perimeter and C80 core coupon series within the predeclared 0.0001 rounding tolerance. This validates transcription and the scalar regression only. The controlling leave-one-out strength error is 25.19 percent and is reported as a non-gated warning. Only 2 of 9 minimum WTC fracture-card requirements and 0 of 9 CF6-80A2/cowling requirements are available. NCSTAR 1-2B also corrects the WTC 1 engine identity to CF6-80A2; JT9D applies to UA175/WTC 2. No OpenRadioss coupon, failure deletion, facade impact, global, thermal or Blender calculation is authorized by V9A.

v9b_key_results.interpretation: V9B reproducibly extracts all nine declared longitudinal M26/C80 vector traces and passes the two axis-calibration and two median property-error gates. The full digitization gate fails because C80_QS has only 25 unique centreline points against a minimum of 30, C80_299 exceeds the 10 percent individual yield and tensile error limits, and C80_401 exceeds the individual yield error limit. No post-hoc filter is added. The conditional non-eroding OpenRadioss coupon, failure deletion and facade impact are not run. Targeted GE, FAA and NASA sources still provide 0 of 9 requirements for a production CF6-80A2/cowling material-fracture card, and no generic alloy is substituted. This is a valid negative evidence result, not a solver failure or physical validation.

v9c_key_results.interpretation: V9C implements the official NIST ringing-aware yield procedure without modifying the immutable V9B traces and retains the unfiltered V9B tensile maxima. Seven of nine curves pass all predeclared gates and C80_QS is recovered. C80_299 remains 13.38 percent high in tensile strength, which the yield polynomial cannot correct, and C80_401 remains 22.34 percent high in yield strength. The original high-rate measurement channels and per-specimen correction windows were not located publicly, so the complete NIST signal reduction cannot be reproduced. V9C is a valid negative revalidation result, not solver failure or physical validation; no coupon or impact calculation is authorized.

v9d_key_results.interpretation: V9D validates only the completeness and provenance of an unsent local access dossier. The dossier names 12 exact M26/C80 specimens, 10 requested record categories and all five original channel families, and it identifies the official NIST FOIA route with explicit partial-release and record-status language. No request is sent and no raw channel is acquired. The public CF6 update identifies GEK 50460 as the CF6-80A/A2 installation manual, but it still supplies 0 of 9 production material/fracture requirements. No solver, failure deletion or impact is executed.
